name: the writer drops the flag
why: Removes lenFlag from the cell record — the shipped defect: html alone cannot carry an attribute on the <td>, so a reopened tracklist has no flags, tints or LENGTH buttons. Must fail on the round-trip test.
grep: reopened tracklist shows the same flags

name: the writer drops the tooltip
why: Keeps the flag but not its explanation. The tint and buttons come back, and the tooltip saying what the gap is does not. The round-trip test compares each cell's kind AND title, so it must fail.
grep: reopened tracklist shows the same flags

name: the writer takes any title, not only the script's own
why: Drops the data-mb-col-tip ownership check. _applyLengthMismatchFlag() always sets the tooltip and the marker together, so on every flagged cell a fixture can produce the check is already true. It guards a cell whose title something else rewrote after flagging, which no fixture does. KNOWN UNCOVERED.

name: the reader accepts any flag value
why: Drops the warn/severe allowlist, so whatever string a hand-edited file holds is written into data-mb-len-flag. Must fail on the tamper test, where 'bogus' then reaches the DOM.

name: the reader accepts a non-string tooltip
why: Drops the typeof check, so an object in lenTip is coerced into the title ('[object Object]') and marked as the script's own. Must fail on the tamper test's second cell.

name: the reader ignores the on/off setting
why: Restores a saved flag even when flagging has been switched off since. Must fail on the switched-off test. That test passed on unfixed code too, since nothing was restored then — this mutation is what makes it load-bearing.

name: the reader does not re-mark the tooltip as the script's own
why: Restores the title without data-mb-col-tip. The first load looks right; a SECOND save then refuses the title (the writer's ownership check) and the second reopen loses it. Must fail on the save-again test, and only there.

name: the multi-table hydrate loop never calls the reader
why: A release tracklist is tableMode 'multi', so this is the loop a Load from Disk takes. Must fail on the round-trip test.
grep: reopened tracklist shows the same flags

name: the single-table hydrate loop never calls the reader
why: The single-table loop serves single-table Load from Disk and the sub-table handoff tab. No pageType that has LENGTH flags reaches it: release-tracks is multi-table and is not in SA_SNAPSHOT_SUPPORTED_PAGETYPES. KNOWN UNREACHABLE today. Kept so that adding the handoff to release-tracks, or flags to a single-table page, finds a reader already in place.
grep: reopened tracklist|saved again|only a known flag
